title.zh: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十七 蹇義 夏原吉
title.en: Volume 149 Biographies 37: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji
title.raw: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十七 蹇義 夏原吉 Volume 149 Biographies 37: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji

sentences.zh: 蹇義夏原吉

translations.literal: Jian Yi; Xia Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji

translations.literal: Opening section bracket 〈
translations.idiomatic: Opening section bracket 〈

sentences.zh: （俞士吉李文郁鄒師顏）〉

translations.literal: (Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, Zou Shiyan)〉
translations.idiomatic: (with appended biographies of Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, and Zou Shiyan)〉

sentences.zh: 燕師入，迎附，遷左侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Yan army entered the capital, he came over and submitted; he was transferred to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan's army entered the capital, Jian Yi went over to his side and was made Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 數月，進尚書。

translations.literal: Several months later, he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 時方務反建文之政，所更易者悉罷之。

translations.literal: At the time the court was bent on reversing the Jianwen administration's policies, and every change that had been made was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then intent on undoing the Jianwen reforms, and every measure that had been altered was struck down.

sentences.zh: 義從容言曰：「損益貴適時宜。

translations.literal: Yi said calmly: "In adding or subtracting from policy, what matters is suiting the times.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi spoke calmly: "Whether to add or cut policy depends on what the times require.

sentences.zh: 前改者固不當，今必欲盡復者，亦未悉當也。

translations.literal: The earlier changes were indeed improper, yet to insist now on restoring everything is also not entirely right."
translations.idiomatic: The earlier reforms were indeed wrong, but to insist on restoring every one of them now would not be right either."

sentences.zh: 」因舉數事陳說本末。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cited several cases and set forth their background from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited several examples and explained how each had come about.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he was made concurrent Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2 he was also appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝有所傳諭太子，輒遣義，能委曲導意。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor had instructions to convey to the heir, he would send Yi, who could tactfully guide the heir to understand the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor wished to convey something to the heir, he sent Jian Yi, who could delicately make the emperor's meaning clear.

sentences.zh: 帝與太子俱愛重之。

translations.literal: Both emperor and heir held him in affection and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and heir alike valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝巡北京，命輔皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor toured Beijing and ordered Yi to assist the crown prince in governing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 the emperor went north to Beijing and left Jian Yi to help the crown prince administer the realm.

sentences.zh: 義熟典故，達治體，軍國事皆倚辦。

translations.literal: Yi was versed in precedent and understood the structure of governance; military and state affairs alike relied on him to handle.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi knew precedent and understood how government worked; both military and civil affairs were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 時舊臣見親用者，戶部尚書夏原吉與義齊名，中外稱曰「蹇、夏」。

translations.literal: Among former officials then in close favor, Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji was equally famed with Yi; within and without the court they were called "Jian and Xia."
translations.idiomatic: Among the veteran ministers then in favor, Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji was Jian Yi's equal in renown; inside and outside court they were known as "Jian and Xia."

sentences.zh: 滿三考，帝親宴二人便殿，褒揚甚至。

translations.literal: When they completed three terms of evaluation, the emperor personally feasted the two men in the side hall and praised them to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: After they completed three triennial reviews, the emperor personally entertained them in a side hall and praised them in the highest terms.

sentences.zh: 數奉命兼理他部事，職務填委，處之裕如。

translations.literal: Repeatedly ordered on commission to administer other ministries as well, with duties piled high, he handled them with ease.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered to take charge of other ministries as well; though his duties piled up, he managed them with ease.

sentences.zh: 十七年以父喪歸，帝及太子皆遣官賜祭。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned home on his father's death; both emperor and heir sent officials with offerings for the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he went home to mourn his father; both emperor and heir sent officials with sacrificial gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔起復。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him to office before mourning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him back to office before his mourning period had ended.

sentences.zh: 十九年，三殿災，敕廷臣二十六人巡行天下。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the three main halls burned; the emperor ordered twenty-six court officials to tour the empire.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 fire destroyed the three main palace halls, and the emperor sent twenty-six court officials to tour the realm.

sentences.zh: 義及給事中馬俊分巡應天諸府，問軍民疾苦，黜文武長吏擾民者數人，條興革數十事奏行之。

translations.literal: Yi and Supervising Secretary Ma Jun divided the inspection of the prefectures under Yingtian, inquiring into the hardships of soldiers and civilians, dismissing several civil and military superiors who harassed the people, and memorializing dozens of items for reform and abolition, which were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi and Supervising Secretary Ma Jun toured the prefectures of the Nanjing region, inquiring into civilian and military grievances, removing several civil and military chiefs who oppressed the people, and memorializing dozens of reforms that were adopted.

sentences.zh: 還治部事。

translations.literal: He returned to administer his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He then resumed his ministry duties.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝北征還，以太子曲宥呂震婿主事張鶴朝參失儀，罪義不匡正，逮義系錦衣衛獄。

translations.literal: The next year, when the emperor returned from the northern campaign, because the heir had bent the rules to excuse Lü Zhen's son-in-law, Director Zhang He, for impropriety at court audience, the emperor blamed Yi for failing to correct the heir and had Yi seized and imprisoned in the Brocade Guard jail.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the emperor returned from his northern campaign, he blamed Jian Yi for not correcting the heir, who had improperly excused Lü Zhen's son-in-law Director Zhang He for a breach of court etiquette at audience, and had Jian Yi thrown into the Brocade Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 又明年春得釋。

translations.literal: In the spring of the year after that he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was released the following spring.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，義、原吉皆以元老為中外所信。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Yi and Yuanji were both trusted within and without as senior statesmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong came to the throne, Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji were both trusted throughout the realm as elder statesmen.

sentences.zh: 帝又念義監國時舊勞，尤厚倚之。

translations.literal: The emperor also recalled Yi's old service when governing the realm and relied on him all the more heavily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also remembered Jian Yi's service while administering the realm and relied on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 首進義少保，賜冠服、象笏、玉帶，兼食二祿。

translations.literal: He first promoted Yi to Junior Guardian, bestowing court dress, an ivory tablet, and a jade belt, with emoluments from two offices.
translations.idiomatic: He first promoted Jian Yi to Junior Guardian, granting him court dress, an ivory tablet, and a jade belt, with the salary of two posts.

sentences.zh: 歷進少師，賜銀章一，文曰「繩愆糾繆」。

translations.literal: He was advanced in turn to Junior Preceptor and given a silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors."
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Junior Preceptor and given a silver seal bearing the words "Correcting faults and remedying errors."

sentences.zh: 已，復賜璽書曰：「曩朕監國，卿以先朝舊臣，日侍左右。

translations.literal: Soon after, the emperor again bestowed an imperial letter saying: "Formerly when I governed the realm, you as an old minister of the previous reign attended me daily at my side.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor sent another sealed letter: "When I was administering the realm, you, as a veteran of the previous reign, attended me every day.

sentences.zh: 兩京肇建，政務方殷，卿勞心焦思，不恤身家，二十余年，夷險一節。

translations.literal: As the two capitals were first being built and state affairs were pressing, you labored in mind and burned in thought, heedless of self and family; for more than twenty years, through ease and peril alike, you held to one standard.
translations.idiomatic: As the two capitals were being built and government was at its busiest, you wore yourself out in service, heedless of your own safety, and for more than twenty years held the same steadfast course through good times and bad.

sentences.zh: 朕承大統，贊襄治理，不懈益恭。

translations.literal: When I inherited the great succession, you assisted in governance, never slackening but growing ever more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne you have aided my rule, never slackening but growing ever more devoted.

sentences.zh: 朕篤念不忘，茲以已意，創制『蹇忠貞印』賜卿。

translations.literal: I hold this deeply in mind and do not forget; now of my own accord I have created the "Jian Loyalty and Integrity Seal" to bestow upon you.
translations.idiomatic: I have never forgotten this, and now of my own accord create and bestow upon you the "Jian Loyalty and Integrity Seal."

sentences.zh: 俾藏於家，傳之後世，知朕君臣共濟艱難，相與有成也。

translations.literal: Keep it in your household and pass it to later generations, so they may know how ruler and minister together crossed hardship and achieved success together."
translations.idiomatic: Keep it in your family and pass it down, so posterity may know how we ruler and minister weathered hardship together and achieved what we did."

sentences.zh: 」時惟楊士奇亦得賜「貞一」印及敕。

translations.literal: At that time only Yang Shiqi also received the gift of a "Integrity and Unity" seal and an edict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only Yang Shiqi also received a "Integrity and Unity" seal and an imperial letter.

sentences.zh: 尋命與英國公輔及原吉同監修《太宗實錄》。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered, together with the Duke of Ying Fu and Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong》.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered, together with the Duke of Ying Zhang Fu and Xia Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the 《Veritable Records of the Yongle Emperor》.

sentences.zh: 義視原吉尤重厚，然過於周慎。

translations.literal: Yi regarded Yuanji with especial weight and warmth, yet he was overly thorough and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi held Xia Yuanji in particular esteem, but he was excessively cautious in his ways.

sentences.zh: 士奇嘗於帝前謂義曰：「何過慮？

translations.literal: Shiqi once said to Yi before the emperor: "Why such excessive worry?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi once said to Jian Yi in the emperor's presence, "Why worry so much?

sentences.zh: 」義曰：「恐鹵莽為後憂耳。

translations.literal: Yi said: "I fear that rashness will become a worry for later."
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi replied, "I fear that carelessness will cause trouble later."

sentences.zh: 」帝兩是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved both views.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with both men.

sentences.zh: 楊榮嘗毀義。

translations.literal: Yang Rong once slandered Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong once spoke ill of Jian Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝不直榮。

translations.literal: The emperor did not side with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not take Rong's side.

sentences.zh: 義頓首言：「榮無他。

translations.literal: Yi kowtowed and said: "Rong has no other motive.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi kowtowed and said, "Rong means no harm.

sentences.zh: 即左右有讒榮者，願陛下慎察。

translations.literal: If those at your side slander Rong, I beg Your Majesty to examine the matter carefully."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone near you speaks against him, I beg Your Majesty to look into it carefully."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「吾固弗信也。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "I never believed it in the first place."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "I never believed it in the first place."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗即位，委寄益重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, his trust in Yi grew still heavier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, his reliance on Jian Yi grew even greater.

sentences.zh: 時方修獻陵，帝欲遵遺詔從儉約，以問義、原吉。

translations.literal: At the time the Xian Mausoleum was under construction; the emperor wished to follow the testamentary edict in practicing frugality and asked Yi and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: While the Xian Mausoleum was being built, the emperor wished to follow his father's testament and keep the work frugal, and consulted Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 二人力贊曰：「聖見高遠，出於至孝，萬世之利也。

translations.literal: The two men strongly endorsed it, saying: "Your sage vision is lofty and far-reaching, springing from utmost filial piety; it is a benefit for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Both men strongly agreed, saying, "Your vision is far-sighted and springs from deepest filial piety; it will benefit generations to come."

sentences.zh: 」帝親為規畫，三月而陵成，宏麗不及長陵，其後諸帝因以為制。

translations.literal: The emperor personally planned it; in three months the mausoleum was completed, its grandeur and splendor not reaching that of the Chang Mausoleum, and later emperors took this as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally oversaw the design; the tomb was finished in three months, less grand than the Chang Mausoleum, and later emperors followed this as the model.

sentences.zh: 迨世宗營永陵，始益崇侈雲。

translations.literal: Only when Emperor Shizong built the Yong Mausoleum did extravagance begin to increase.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Jiajing Emperor built the Yong Mausoleum did tombs grow more lavish.

sentences.zh: 帝征樂安，義、原吉及諸學士皆從，預軍中機務，賜鞍馬甲胄弓劍。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Le'an, Yi, Yuanji, and the various academicians all followed, taking part in military affairs, and were granted saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Le'an, Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, and the Hanlin academicians accompanied him, advising on military affairs, and were given saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.

sentences.zh: 及還，賚予甚厚。

translations.literal: When they returned, rewards and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: On their return he rewarded them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 三年從巡邊還。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned from accompanying the border tour.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he returned from accompanying the emperor on a border inspection.

sentences.zh: 帝以義、原吉、士奇、榮四人者皆已老，賜璽書曰：「卿等皆祖宗遺老，畀輔朕躬。

translations.literal: Because Yi, Yuanji, Shiqi, and Rong were all already old, the emperor bestowed a sealed letter saying: "You are all surviving elders left by our forefathers, entrusted to assist my person.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, Yang Shiqi, and Yang Rong were all advanced in years, the emperor sent a sealed letter: "You are all veterans left by my forefathers to assist me.

sentences.zh: 今黃髮危齒，不宜復典冗劇，傷朝廷優老待賢之禮。

translations.literal: Now with yellow hair and tottering teeth, you should not again preside over tedious and pressing duties, which would harm the court's ritual of honoring age and treating the worthy well.
translations.idiomatic: With your hair white and your teeth failing, you should no longer bear heavy administrative burdens, lest the court fail in its duty to honor age and esteem talent.

sentences.zh: 可輟所務，朝夕在朕左右討論至理，共寧邦家。

translations.literal: You may set aside your duties and morning and evening be at my left and right to discuss ultimate principles and together bring peace to state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Lay aside your offices and stay at my side day and night to discuss great matters and help secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 官祿悉如舊。

translations.literal: Official rank and salary shall all remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Your rank and salary shall remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」明年，郭琎代為尚書。

translations.literal: The next year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Guo Jin replaced him as minister.

sentences.zh: 尋以胡濙言，命義等四人議天下官吏軍民建言章奏。

translations.literal: Before long, on Hu Ying's recommendation, the emperor ordered Yi and the other four men to deliberate on memorials and proposals submitted by officials, soldiers, and civilians throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Hu Ying's advice, he ordered Jian Yi and the other three to review memorials submitted by officials, soldiers, and commoners throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 復賜義銀章，文曰「忠厚寬宏」。

translations.literal: He again bestowed on Yi a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."
translations.idiomatic: He again gave Jian Yi a silver seal bearing the words "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."

sentences.zh: 七年詔有司為義營新第於文明門內。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the relevant offices to build Yi a new residence inside the Gate of Civilization.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 an edict ordered officials to build Jian Yi a new residence inside the Gate of Civilization.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，齋宿得疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Yi fell ill while observing abstention and lodging for ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, Jian Yi fell ill while keeping ritual abstinence.

sentences.zh: 遣醫往視，問所欲言。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a physician to examine him and asked what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a physician and asked if he had anything to say.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下初嗣大寶，望敬守祖宗成憲，始終不渝耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty has newly inherited the great treasure; I hope you will respectfully uphold the settled statutes of the ancestors, from beginning to end without change."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty has just taken the throne; I beg you to reverently uphold our ancestors' established institutions and never waver from them."

sentences.zh: 」遂卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He then died, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚忠定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous title Loyal and Steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 義為人質直孝友，善處僚友間，未嘗一語傷物。

translations.literal: Yi as a man was plain, upright, filial, and friendly; he was skilled in dealings among colleagues and never once spoke a word that wounded others.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi was plainspoken, upright, filial, and friendly; he handled colleagues well and never spoke a hurtful word.

sentences.zh: 士奇常言：「張詠之不飾玩好，傅堯俞之遇人以誠，範景仁之不設城府，義兼有之。

translations.literal: Shiqi often said: "Zhang Yong's not adorning himself with curios, Fu Yaoyu's treating people with sincerity, Fan Jingren's not setting up inner and outer cities in his heart—Yi combines them all."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi often said, "Zhang Yong's freedom from vanity, Fu Yaoyu's sincerity with others, and Fan Jingren's guilelessness—Jian Yi has them all."

sentences.zh: 」子英，有詩名，以蔭為尚寶司丞，歷官太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Ying had a reputation in poetry; through hereditary privilege he became Vice Director of the Directorate of Ceremonial, and rose through offices to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying was known as a poet; through hereditary privilege he became a vice director in the Directorate of Ceremonial and eventually rose to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 夏原吉，字維喆，其先德興人。

translations.literal: Xia Yuanji, styled Weizhe, was by ancestry a man of Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji, courtesy name Weizhe, was descended from a family of Dexing.

sentences.zh: 父時敏，官湘陰教諭，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Shimin held office as instructor in Xiangyin and thereupon made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shimin served as instructor in Xiangyin, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 原吉早孤，力學養母。

translations.literal: Yuanji was orphaned early; he applied himself to learning and supported his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji lost his father young, studied hard, and supported his mother.

sentences.zh: 以鄉薦入太學，選入禁中書制誥。

translations.literal: Recommended from his district, he entered the Imperial Academy and was selected to draft edicts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended from his home district, he entered the Imperial Academy and was chosen to draft edicts in the palace.

sentences.zh: 諸生或喧笑，原吉危坐儼然。

translations.literal: When the students sometimes laughed and made noise, Yuanji sat upright in formal posture.
translations.idiomatic: While other students laughed and talked, Yuanji sat upright and composed.

sentences.zh: 太祖诇而異之。

translations.literal: Taizu observed this and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu noticed and was impressed.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 曹務叢脞，處之悉有條理，尚書郁新甚重之。

translations.literal: Office business was tangled and piled; he handled it all with order, and Minister Yu Xin greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Though ministry business was tangled and heavy, he handled everything in good order, and Minister Yu Xin valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 有劉郎中者，忌其能。

translations.literal: There was a Bureau Director Liu who resented his ability.
translations.idiomatic: A bureau director surnamed Liu resented his talent.

sentences.zh: 會新劾諸司怠事者。

translations.literal: It happened that Xin impeached those in various offices who were slack in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu Xin impeached officials in various offices for neglecting their duties.

sentences.zh: 帝欲宥之，新持不可。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to pardon them; Xin insisted that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to pardon them, but Yu Xin refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，問：「誰教若？

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and asked: "Who taught you to do this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and demanded, "Who put you up to this?

sentences.zh: 」新頓首曰：「堂後書算生。

translations.literal: Xin kowtowed and said: "The clerks and calculators behind the hall."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin kowtowed and said, "The clerks behind the hall."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃下書算生於獄。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon sent the clerks and calculators to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the clerks thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 劉郎中遂言：「教尚書者，原吉也。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Liu then said: "The one who instructed the Minister was Yuanji."
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu then said, "It was Yuanji who advised the minister."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「原吉能佐尚書理部事，汝欲陷之耶！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yuanji can assist the Minister in administering ministry affairs—do you wish to entrap him!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yuanji helps the minister run this ministry—are you trying to frame him!"

sentences.zh: 」劉郎中與書算生皆棄市。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Liu and the clerks and calculators were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu and the clerks were all executed in public.

sentences.zh: 建文初，擢戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign he was made Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年充采訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Investigating Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed an investigating commissioner.

sentences.zh: 巡福建，所過郡邑，核吏治，咨民隱。

translations.literal: Touring Fujian, in every prefecture and county he passed through he examined official governance and inquired into the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Fujian, he examined local governance and heard the people's grievances in every prefecture and county he visited.

sentences.zh: 人皆悅服。

translations.literal: People all rejoiced and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The people were won over.

sentences.zh: 久之，移駐蘄州。

translations.literal: After a long while he shifted his station to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he moved his headquarters to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，或執原吉以獻。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu took the throne, some seized Yuanji to present him as a captive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, some seized Xia Yuanji to hand him over as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 帝釋之，轉左侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor released him and transferred him to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released him and made him Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 或言原吉建文時用事，不可信。

translations.literal: Some said that Yuanji had held power under Jianwen and could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that because Xia Yuanji had held office under Jianwen he could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，與蹇義同進尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen and promoted him to Minister together with Jian Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it and promoted him to minister alongside Jian Yi.

sentences.zh: 偕義等詳定賦役諸制。

translations.literal: Together with Yi and others he worked out in detail the various regulations on taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Jian Yi and others he worked out the regulations on taxes and corvée labor in detail.

sentences.zh: 建白三十余事，皆簡便易遵守。

translations.literal: He proposed more than thirty measures, all simple, convenient, and easy to observe.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed more than thirty reforms, all simple and easy to follow.

sentences.zh: 曰：「行之而難繼者，且重困民，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: He said: "Those that in practice would be hard to sustain and would moreover heavily burden the people—I cannot bear to propose them."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I will not propose measures that would be hard to sustain and would only burden the people further."

sentences.zh: 」浙西大水，有司治不效。

translations.literal: Western Zhejiang suffered great floods; the local offices' remedies were ineffective.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang suffered severe flooding, and local officials could not cope.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，命原吉治之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the emperor ordered Yuanji to remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 1 the emperor put Xia Yuanji in charge of relief.

sentences.zh: 尋命侍郎李文郁為之副，復使僉都御史俞士吉賫水利書賜之。

translations.literal: Before long Vice Minister Li Wenyu was appointed his deputy, and Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again sent to present him with books on water control as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Vice Minister Li Wenyu was appointed his deputy, and Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was sent with books on waterworks as imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 原吉請循禹三江入海故跡，浚吳淞下流，上接太湖，而度地為閘，以時蓄泄。

translations.literal: Yuanji requested to follow the old traces by which Yu's three rivers entered the sea, dredge the lower reaches of the Wusong, connect upward to Lake Tai, and according to the terrain build sluice gates to store and release water at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji proposed following the ancient course of Yu's three rivers to the sea, dredging the lower Wusong to link with Lake Tai, and building sluice gates at suitable points to regulate storage and release.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 役十余萬人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand men were put to labor.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand laborers were mobilized.

sentences.zh: 原吉布衣徒步，日夜經畫。

translations.literal: Yuanji wore plain cloth and went on foot, planning day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji wore plain clothes and went on foot, planning the work day and night.

sentences.zh: 盛暑不張蓋，曰：「民勞，吾何忍獨適。

translations.literal: In the height of summer he would not raise a canopy, saying: "The people labor—how can I bear to enjoy comfort alone?
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer he refused a parasol, saying, "The people are toiling—how can I enjoy comfort alone?

sentences.zh: 」事竣，還京師，言水雖由故道入海，而支流未盡疏泄，非經久計。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he returned to the capital and said that although the water now entered the sea by the old channel, the tributary streams had not all been dredged and released, and this was not a plan for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done he returned to the capital and reported that although water now reached the sea by the old channel, tributary streams were still not fully cleared—a short-term fix, not a lasting solution.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，原吉復行，浚白茆塘、劉家河、大黃浦。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Yuanji went out again and dredged the Baimao Pond, the Liu Family River, and the Great Huangpu.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month Xia Yuanji went out again to dredge the Baimao Pond, the Liu Family River, and the Great Huangpu.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿袁復為之副。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 已，復命陜西參政宋性佐之。

translations.literal: Before long the Shaanxi Administration Vice Commissioner Song Xing was again ordered to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Shaanxi administration vice commissioner Song Xing was sent to assist him as well.

sentences.zh: 九月工畢，水泄，蘇、松農田大利。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the work was completed, the water drained off, and the farmland of Suzhou and Songjiang greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month the work was finished, the waters drained, and farmland in Suzhou and Songjiang benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 三年還。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he returned.

sentences.zh: 其夏，浙西大饑。

translations.literal: That summer western Zhejiang suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That summer western Zhejiang suffered severe famine.

sentences.zh: 命原吉率俞士吉、袁復及左通政趙居任往振，發粟三十萬石，給牛種。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yuanji to lead Yu Shiji, Yuan Fu, and Left Administration Commissioner Zhao Juren to provide relief, issuing three hundred thousand piculs of grain and supplying oxen and seed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xia Yuanji with Yu Shiji, Yuan Fu, and Left Administration Commissioner Zhao Juren to provide relief, distributing three hundred thousand piculs of grain and supplying oxen and seed.

sentences.zh: 有請召民佃水退淤田益賦者，原吉馳疏止之。

translations.literal: Some proposed summoning the people to tenant silt fields left when the water receded and increasing the tax assessment; Yuanji sent an urgent memorial to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed recruiting peasants to farm reclaimed silt land and raise the tax assessment, Xia Yuanji sent an urgent memorial to stop it.

sentences.zh: 姚廣孝還自浙西，稱原吉曰：「古之遺愛也。

translations.literal: Yao Guangxiao returned from western Zhejiang and praised Yuanji, saying: "A man who leaves enduring love as in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guangxiao returned from western Zhejiang and said of Xia Yuanji, "He is a man of enduring benevolence such as antiquity knew."

sentences.zh: 」亡何，郁新卒，召還，理部事。

translations.literal: Before long Yu Xin died; Yuanji was recalled to administer ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu Xin died, and Xia Yuanji was recalled to run the ministry.

sentences.zh: 首請裁冗食，平賦役；

translations.literal: He first requested cutting redundant consumption and leveling taxes and corvée;
translations.idiomatic: He first proposed cutting redundant expenditures and equalizing taxes and corvée labor;

sentences.zh: 嚴鹽法、錢鈔之禁；

translations.literal: strict enforcement of the salt laws and prohibitions on paper money;
translations.idiomatic: strict enforcement of salt laws and prohibitions on paper money;

sentences.zh: 清倉場，廣屯種，以給邊蘇民，且便商賈。

translations.literal: clearing the granaries and depots, expanding military colonies and planting, to supply the borders and relieve the people, and also to facilitate merchants.
translations.idiomatic: clearing granaries, expanding military colonies to supply the frontiers and ease the people's burdens, and facilitating trade.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 凡中外戶口、府庫、田賦贏縮之數，各以小簡書置懷中，時檢閱之。

translations.literal: For all figures on households within and without, treasuries and storehouses, and surpluses and deficits in land tax, he kept each on small slips in his bosom and reviewed them from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: He kept slips in his pocket recording household counts, treasury balances, and land-tax surpluses and deficits throughout the realm, and reviewed them constantly.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝問：「天下錢、谷幾何？

translations.literal: One day the emperor asked: "How much money and grain are there in the realm?
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor asked, "How much money and grain does the realm hold?

sentences.zh: 」對甚悉，以是益重之。

translations.literal: He answered in great detail, and for this reason the emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He answered in full detail, and the emperor valued him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 當是時，兵革初定，論「靖難」功臣封賞，分封諸藩，增設武衛百司。

translations.literal: At that time, when the weapons of war had just been laid down, rewards and enfeoffments for meritorious ministers of the Pacification were debated, princely fiefs were apportioned, and military guards and the hundred offices were increased.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, with the realm newly pacified after the civil war, the court debated rewards for supporters of the Yongle succession, enfeoffed imperial princes, and expanded military guards and government offices.

sentences.zh: 已，又發卒八十萬問罪安南、中官造巨艦通海外諸國、大起北都宮闕。

translations.literal: Before long troops numbering eight hundred thousand were again raised to punish Annam, eunuchs built great ships to reach the various countries beyond the seas, and the palace halls of the Northern Capital were raised on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Then eight hundred thousand troops were sent to punish Annam, eunuchs built great ships to reach overseas countries, and construction of the Northern Capital palaces began on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 供億轉輸以鉅萬萬計，皆取給戶曹。

translations.literal: Supplies and transport costs ran to tens of millions upon millions, all drawn from the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies and transport costs ran into the tens of millions, all drawn from the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 原吉悉心計應之，國用不絀。

translations.literal: Yuanji with full heart calculated and met them; state expenditure did not fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji planned carefully to meet every demand, and state finances never ran short.

sentences.zh: 六年命督軍民輸材北都，詔以錦衣官校從，治怠事者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to supervise soldiers and civilians transporting materials to the Northern Capital; an edict sent Brocade Guard officers to follow him and punish those slack in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was ordered to supervise the transport of building materials to the Northern Capital, with Brocade Guard officers authorized to punish slack workers.

sentences.zh: 原吉慮犯者眾，告戒而後行，人皆感悅。

translations.literal: Yuanji feared that offenders would be many; he gave warnings before setting out, and people all were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing many would be punished, Xia Yuanji warned the workers beforehand, and they were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝北巡，命兼攝行在禮部、兵部、都察院事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor toured the north and ordered him concurrently to take charge of the traveling Ministry of Rites, Ministry of War, and Censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 the emperor toured the north and left him in charge of the traveling ministries of Rites and War and the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 有二指揮冒月廩，帝欲斬之。

translations.literal: Two commanders had fraudulently drawn monthly rations; the emperor wished to behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Two commanders had fraudulently drawn monthly rations, and the emperor wanted them executed.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「非律也，假實為盜，將何以加？

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "This is not according to law; if false claims are treated as theft, what further penalty can be added?
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said, "That is not lawful; if false claims are treated as theft, what further penalty could there be?

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，輔太孫留守北京，總行在九卿事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor campaigned north; Yuanji assisted the heir apparent in remaining to guard Beijing and oversaw the affairs of the nine ministers at the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the emperor campaigned north, leaving Xia Yuanji to assist the heir apparent in guarding Beijing and oversee the traveling court's nine ministries.

sentences.zh: 時諸司草創，每旦，原吉入佐太孫參決庶務。

translations.literal: At that time the various offices were newly established; each morning Yuanji entered to assist the heir in deciding routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With the offices still being set up, each morning Xia Yuanji helped the heir decide routine affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝退，諸曹郎御史環請事。

translations.literal: After court was dismissed, bureau directors, section heads, and censors surrounded him requesting decisions.
translations.idiomatic: After court, bureau directors and censors crowded around him with questions.

sentences.zh: 原吉口答手書，不動聲色。

translations.literal: Yuanji answered by mouth and wrote by hand, without change of voice or expression.
translations.idiomatic: He answered orally and wrote replies without changing expression.

sentences.zh: 北達行在，南啟監國，京師肅然。

translations.literal: Northward he reached the traveling court; southward he reported to the regency; the capital was orderly and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He reported north to the traveling court and south to the regency in Nanjing, and both capitals ran in good order.

sentences.zh: 帝還，賜鈔幣、鞍馬、牢醴，慰勞有加。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he bestowed paper money, saddles and horses, and provisions for sacrifice, with extra consolation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he rewarded him with paper money, horses, and provisions, with special words of thanks.

sentences.zh: 尋從還南京，命侍太孫周行鄉落，觀民間疾苦。

translations.literal: Before long he followed the emperor back to Nanjing and was ordered to attend the heir on a tour of villages and hamlets to observe the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he accompanied the emperor back to Nanjing and was ordered to accompany the heir on a tour of villages to see the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 原吉取齏黍以進，曰：「願殿下食此，知民艱。

translations.literal: Yuanji took pickled grain and presented it, saying: "I hope Your Highness will eat this and know the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji brought coarse pickled grain for the heir to taste, saying, "I hope Your Highness will eat this and know the people's hardship.

sentences.zh: 」九載滿，與蹇義皆宴便殿，帝指二人謂群臣曰：「高皇帝養賢以貽朕。

translations.literal: When nine years of service were complete, he and Jian Yi were both feasted in the side hall; the emperor pointed to the two men and said to the assembled ministers: "The High Emperor nurtured worthies to bequeath to me.
translations.idiomatic: When nine years of service were complete, he and Jian Yi were feasted in a side hall; the emperor pointed to them and told the ministers, "Taizu nurtured worthy men for my sake.

sentences.zh: 欲觀古名臣，此其人矣。

translations.literal: If you wish to see famous ministers of antiquity, these are the men."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to see the great ministers of old, here they are."

sentences.zh: 」自是屢侍太孫，往來兩京，在道隨事納忠，多所裨益。

translations.literal: From then on he repeatedly attended the heir, traveling between the two capitals; on the road he offered loyal counsel as occasions arose, with much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he often attended the heir, traveling between the two capitals and offering loyal counsel along the way to great effect.

sentences.zh: 十八年，北京宮室成，使原吉南召太子、太孫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Beijing palace halls were completed, Yuanji was sent south to summon the crown prince and heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, when the Beijing palaces were completed, Xia Yuanji was sent south to summon the crown prince and heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 既還，原吉言：「連歲營建，今告成。

translations.literal: After he returned, Yuanji said: "For successive years we have built; now the work is announced complete.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Xia Yuanji said, "Construction has gone on for years; it is now finished.

sentences.zh: 宜撫流亡，蠲逋負以寬民力。

translations.literal: We should comfort the displaced and wandering, and remit arrears to ease the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: We should resettle refugees, remit tax arrears, and ease the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: 」明年，三殿災，原吉復申前請，亟命所司行之。

translations.literal: The next year the three halls burned; Yuanji again submitted his earlier request, and the emperor urgently ordered the relevant offices to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when fire destroyed the three main halls, Xia Yuanji repeated his proposal, and the emperor immediately ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 初以殿災詔求直言，群臣多言都北京非便。

translations.literal: At first, because of the hall fire an edict sought blunt counsel; many among the ministers said that making Beijing the capital was not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall fire prompted an edict calling for frank counsel, many ministers argued that moving the capital to Beijing had been a mistake.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，殺主事蕭儀，曰：「方遷都時，與大臣密議，久而後定，非輕舉也。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and killed Director Xiao Yi, saying: "When we were moving the capital, I secretly deliberated with the great ministers; only after a long time was it settled—it was no light undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and executed Director Xiao Yi, saying, "When we moved the capital I deliberated at length with my senior ministers; it was no hasty decision.

sentences.zh: 」言者因劾大臣。

translations.literal: The memorialists thereupon impeached the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The memorialists then impeached the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝命跪午門外質辨。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them to kneel outside the Meridian Gate and debate the charges.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to kneel outside the Meridian Gate and debate the charges face to face.

sentences.zh: 大臣爭詈言者，原吉獨奏曰：「彼應詔無罪。

translations.literal: The great ministers quarreled and reviled the memorialists; Yuanji alone memorialized, saying: "They responded to the edict and are without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The senior ministers quarreled with the memorialists, but Xia Yuanji alone memorialized, "They answered the edict and are not guilty.

sentences.zh: 臣等備員大臣，不能協贊大計，罪在臣等。

translations.literal: We who fill posts as great ministers could not jointly assist the great plan—the guilt lies with us."
translations.idiomatic: We senior ministers failed to support your great design—the fault is ours."

sentences.zh: 」帝意解，兩宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was eased and he pardoned both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and pardoned both sides.

sentences.zh: 或尤原吉背初議。

translations.literal: Some blamed Yuanji for betraying the initial agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Some blamed Xia Yuanji for going back on the ministers' earlier position.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾輩歷事久，言雖失，幸上憐之。

translations.literal: He said: "We have served long; though our words were mistaken, fortunately the sovereign pities us.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "We have served long; though we were wrong, the emperor may yet show mercy.

sentences.zh: 若言官得罪，所損不細矣。

translations.literal: If censors who speak out are punished, the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: If remonstrating officials are punished, the harm will be far greater."

sentences.zh: 」眾始嘆服。

translations.literal: The assembly then sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did his colleagues admire him.

sentences.zh: 原吉雖居戶部，國家大事輒令詳議。

translations.literal: Although Yuanji held office in the Revenue Ministry, whenever there were great affairs of state he was ordered to deliberate on them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xia Yuanji headed the Ministry of Revenue, he was routinely consulted on major state affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝每禦便殿闕門，召語移時，左右莫得聞。

translations.literal: The emperor would often hold court in the side hall at the palace gate and summon him to talk for a long while; those at his side could not hear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often received him in a side hall and talked with him at length, out of earshot of attendants.

sentences.zh: 退則恂恂若無預者。

translations.literal: When he withdrew he was respectful and cautious as if he had taken no part.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he behaved with modest deference, as if he had played no special role.

sentences.zh: 交阯平，帝問：「遷官與賞孰便？

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi was pacified, the emperor asked: "Which is more advantageous, promoting officials or giving rewards?
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi was pacified, the emperor asked, "Which is better, promoting officials or giving rewards?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「賞費於一時，有限；

translations.literal: He answered: "Rewards cost only for a moment and are limited;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Rewards are a one-time cost and limited;

sentences.zh: 遷官為後日費，無窮也。

translations.literal: promoting officials is a cost for later days and is endless."
translations.idiomatic: promotions burden the treasury forever."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice.

sentences.zh: 西域法王來朝，帝欲郊勞，原吉不可。

translations.literal: When a Buddhist king-lawgiver from the Western Regions came to court, the emperor wished to greet him with suburban rites; Yuanji disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: When a Buddhist king from the Western Regions came to court, the emperor wished to greet him with suburban rites; Xia Yuanji objected.

sentences.zh: 及法王入，原吉見，不拜。

translations.literal: When the king-lawgiver entered, Yuanji saw him but did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the king entered, Xia Yuanji met him but did not bow.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿欲效韓愈耶？

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Do you wish to imitate Han Yu?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Are you trying to imitate Han Yu?

sentences.zh: 」山東唐賽兒反，事平，俘脅從者三千余人至。

translations.literal: Tang Sai'er rebelled in Shandong; when the affair was settled, more than three thousand coerced followers who had been captured were brought in.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Sai'er rebelled in Shandong and was defeated, more than three thousand coerced followers were brought in as captives.

sentences.zh: 原吉請於帝，悉原之。

translations.literal: Yuanji requested of the emperor that they all be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji asked the emperor to pardon them all.

sentences.zh: 谷王叛，帝疑長沙有通謀者。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gu rebelled; the emperor suspected that at Changsha there were those in secret collusion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gu rebelled, the emperor suspected collusion in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 原吉以百口保之，乃得寢。

translations.literal: Yuanji guaranteed them with the lives of a hundred mouths, and the matter was then laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji pledged his family's lives on their innocence, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十九年冬，帝將大舉征沙漠。

translations.literal: In the winter of the nineteenth year the emperor was about to launch a great campaign against the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year 19 the emperor planned a major campaign into the steppe.

sentences.zh: 命原吉與禮部尚書呂震、兵部尚書方賓、工部尚書吳中等議，皆言兵不當出。

translations.literal: He ordered Yuanji, together with Minister of Rites Lü Zhen, Minister of War Fang Bin, Minister of Works Wu Zhong, and others to deliberate; all said the army should not go out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xia Yuanji, Ministers Lü Zhen of Rites, Fang Bin of War, and Wu Zhong of Works, among others, to deliberate; all said the army should not march.

sentences.zh: 未奏，會帝召賓，賓力言軍興費乏，帝不懌。

translations.literal: Before they could memorialize, it happened that the emperor summoned Bin; Bin spoke forcefully that military mobilization was costly and supplies were lacking, and the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could memorialize, the emperor summoned Fang Bin, who argued forcefully that war would strain supplies; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 召原吉問邊儲多寡，對曰：「比年師出無功，軍馬儲蓄十喪八九，災眚叠作，內外俱疲。

translations.literal: He summoned Yuanji and asked how much border storage there was; Yuanji answered: "In recent years when armies went out they achieved nothing; military stores of horses and supplies are nine-tenths gone; disasters and portents come in succession; within and without all are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Xia Yuanji and asked about border stores. Xia Yuanji answered, "Campaigns in recent years have achieved nothing; nine-tenths of military stores are gone; disasters follow one another; court and country alike are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 況聖躬少安，尚須調護，乞遣將往征，勿勞車駕。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Sacred Person has only lately been at ease and still needs care and nursing; I beg that generals be sent on campaign and that the imperial carriage not be troubled."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty has only lately recovered and still needs care; I beg you to send generals instead and not take the field yourself."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，立命原吉出理開平糧儲。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and immediately ordered Yuanji out to manage grain stores at Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and immediately sent Xia Yuanji to manage grain stores at Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 而吳中入對如賓言，帝益怒。

translations.literal: When Wu Zhong entered for audience and spoke as Bin had, the emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zhong spoke to the emperor as Fang Bin had, the emperor grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 召原吉系之內官監，並系大理丞鄒師顏，以嘗署戶部也。

translations.literal: He summoned Yuanji and imprisoned him in the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs, and also imprisoned Assistant Minister of Justice Zou Shiyan, because he had once signed for the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xia Yuanji imprisoned in the eunuch directorate and also imprisoned Assistant Minister of Justice Zou Shiyan, who had once signed ministry documents.

sentences.zh: 賓懼自殺。

translations.literal: Bin, in fear, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bin, in fear, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 遂並籍原吉家，自賜鈔外，惟布衣瓦器。

translations.literal: Thereupon they also inventoried Yuanji's household; apart from paper money bestowed by the emperor, there were only plain cloth and earthenware vessels.
translations.idiomatic: They inventoried his household and found nothing but plain clothes and earthenware vessels, apart from paper money the emperor had given him.

sentences.zh: 明年北征，以糧盡引還。

translations.literal: The next year on the northern campaign, because grain was exhausted they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the northern campaign turned back for lack of supplies.

sentences.zh: 已，復連歲出塞，皆不見敵。

translations.literal: Before long, for successive years they went beyond the passes, yet never saw the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: For years afterward campaigns beyond the frontier found no enemy.

sentences.zh: 還至榆木川，帝不豫，顧左右曰：「夏原吉愛我。

translations.literal: Returning to the Elm River region, the emperor was unwell and turned to those at his side, saying: "Xia Yuanji loves me.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the Elm River, the emperor fell ill and said to those around him, "Xia Yuanji loved me.

sentences.zh: 」崩聞至之三日，太子走系所，呼原吉，哭而告之。

translations.literal: Three days after news of his death arrived, the heir ran to the place of imprisonment, called Yuanji, and weeping told him.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after news of the death arrived, the heir ran to the prison, called out Xia Yuanji, and weeping told him the news.

sentences.zh: 原吉伏地哭，不能起。

translations.literal: Yuanji lay prostrate weeping and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji lay prostrate weeping and could not rise.

sentences.zh: 太子令出獄，與議喪禮，復問赦詔所宜。

translations.literal: The heir ordered him released from prison to deliberate on funeral rites, and again asked what should be in the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: The heir ordered him released to help plan the funeral and asked what the amnesty edict should include.

sentences.zh: 對以振饑、省賦役、罷西洋取寶船及雲南、交阯采辦諸道金銀課。

translations.literal: He answered with relief for famine, reduction of taxes and corvée, abolition of treasure ships to the Western Ocean, and cessation of gold and silver levies on the procurement routes in Yunnan and Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed famine relief, tax reductions, ending treasure voyages to the Western Ocean, and halting gold and silver levies from Yunnan and Jiaozhi procurement.

sentences.zh: 悉從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: The heir adopted every recommendation.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，復其官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong came to the throne, he was reinstated in office.

sentences.zh: 方原吉在獄，有母喪，至是乞歸終制。

translations.literal: While Yuanji was in prison his mother died; at this time he requested to return and complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: While Xia Yuanji was in prison his mother had died; he now asked to return home to complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿老臣，當與朕共濟艱難。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are an old minister and ought to cross hardship together with me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are an elder minister; you should share hardship with me.

sentences.zh: 卿有喪，朕獨無喪乎？

translations.literal: You have a bereavement—am I alone without bereavement?
translations.idiomatic: You have lost your mother—have I not lost a parent as well?

sentences.zh: 」厚賜之，令家人護喪，馳傳歸葬，有司治喪事。

translations.literal: He richly rewarded him, ordered his family to escort the coffin, sent post relays for the return burial, and had the relevant offices manage funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him generous gifts, sent his family to escort the coffin home by relay post, and ordered officials to manage the funeral.

sentences.zh: 原吉不敢復言。

translations.literal: Yuanji did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji did not dare raise the matter again.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 呂震以太子少師班原吉上，帝命鴻臚引震列其下。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen, as Junior Preceptor of the Heir, ranked above Yuanji; the emperor ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to lead Zhen to stand below him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen, as Junior Preceptor of the Heir, ranked above Xia Yuanji; the emperor ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to place Lü Zhen below him instead.

sentences.zh: 進少保，兼太子少傅、尚書如故，食三祿。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Junior Guardian, concurrently Junior Tutor of the Heir and Minister as before, with emoluments from three offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian, retaining his posts as Junior Tutor of the Heir and minister, with the salary of three offices.

sentences.zh: 原吉固辭，乃聽辭太子少傅祿。

translations.literal: Yuanji firmly declined; only then was he permitted to decline the salary of Junior Tutor of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji firmly declined, and the emperor allowed him to give up the salary of Junior Tutor of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 賜「繩愆糾繆」銀章，建第於兩京。

translations.literal: He was given a silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors" and residences were built for him in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He received a silver seal bearing the words "Correcting faults and remedying errors," and mansions were built for him in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 已而仁宗崩，太子至自南京。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Renzong died, and the crown prince arrived from Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Renzong died, and the crown prince came up from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 原吉奉遺詔迎於盧溝橋。

translations.literal: Yuanji, following the testamentary edict, welcomed him at the Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Following the testamentary edict, Xia Yuanji welcomed him at the Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，以舊輔益親重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, as an old assistant he was all the more treated with intimacy and weight.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he treated this veteran counselor with even greater intimacy and trust.

sentences.zh: 明年，漢王高煦反，亦以「靖難」為辭，移檄罪狀諸大臣，以原吉為首。

translations.literal: The next year the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, rebelled, likewise taking the Pacification as his pretext, and issued a proclamation listing the crimes of the great ministers, with Yuanji named first.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, rebelled, likewise invoking the Pacification, and issued a proclamation denouncing the senior ministers, with Xia Yuanji listed first.

sentences.zh: 帝夜召諸臣議。

translations.literal: At night the emperor summoned the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned his ministers for a night council.

sentences.zh: 楊榮首勸帝親征。

translations.literal: Yang Rong was the first to urge the emperor to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong was the first to urge the emperor to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 帝難之。

translations.literal: The emperor found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「獨不見李景隆已事耶？

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "Have you alone not seen what became of Li Jinglong?
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said, "Have you forgotten what became of Li Jinglong?

sentences.zh: 臣昨見所遣將，命下即色變，臨事可知矣。

translations.literal: Yesterday I saw the generals you sent out; the moment the order was given their faces changed color—how they will fare when action comes can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I saw the generals you dispatched; the moment they received orders their faces fell—you can guess how they will perform in battle.

sentences.zh: 且兵貴神速，卷甲趨之，所謂先人有奪人之心也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in warfare speed is prized; roll up armor and hurry there—this is what is called the ancients seizing men's hearts first.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, war favors speed; march at once in full armor—that is how you seize the initiative.

sentences.zh: 榮策善。

translations.literal: Rong's plan is good.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's plan is sound.

sentences.zh: 」帝意遂決。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 師還，賚予加等，賜閽者三人。

translations.literal: When the army returned, rewards and gifts were increased by a grade, and three gatekeepers were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, rewards were increased and he was given three gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 原吉以無功辭。

translations.literal: Yuanji declined on the grounds of having no merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji declined on the grounds that he had done nothing to deserve them.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 三年，從北巡。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he accompanied the northern tour.

sentences.zh: 帝取原吉橐糗嘗之，笑曰：「何惡也？

translations.literal: The emperor took the dried grain from Yuanji's pouch and tasted it, laughing: "How vile!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the dried grain from Xia Yuanji's pouch and tasted it, laughing, "How foul!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「軍中猶有餒者。

translations.literal: Yuanji answered: "In the army there are still men who go hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "There are still hungry men in the army.

sentences.zh: 」帝命賜以大官之饌，且犒將士。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that he be given food from the imperial kitchen and that the generals and soldiers be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered imperial provisions for him and rewards for the troops.

sentences.zh: 從閱武兔兒山，帝怒諸將慢，褫其衣。

translations.literal: Following the military review at Tuer Mountain, the emperor was angry that the generals were slack and stripped off their garments.
translations.idiomatic: At a military review on Tuer Mountain the emperor, angered by the generals' slackness, had their coats stripped off.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「將帥，國爪牙，奈何凍而斃之？

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "Generals and commanders are the claws and teeth of the state—how can we freeze them to death?
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said, "Generals are the state's claws and teeth—how can we let them freeze to death?

sentences.zh: 」反覆力諫。

translations.literal: He remonstrated repeatedly with force.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為卿釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For your sake I release them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For your sake I will release them.

sentences.zh: 」再與蹇義同賜銀印，文曰：「含弘貞靖。

translations.literal: Again he and Jian Yi were together given silver seals inscribed: "Broad, tolerant, upright, and tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: He and Jian Yi were again given silver seals bearing the words "Broad, tolerant, upright, and tranquil."

sentences.zh: 」帝雅善繪事，嘗親畫《壽星圖》以賜。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature skilled at painting and once personally painted the "Picture of the Star of Longevity" to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was an accomplished painter and once personally painted the "Picture of the Star of Longevity" as a gift.

sentences.zh: 其他圖畫、服食、器用、銀幣、玩好之賜，無虛日。

translations.literal: Other gifts of paintings, food and drink, utensils, silver money, and curios—there was no day without them.
translations.idiomatic: Other gifts of paintings, food, utensils, silver, and curios came almost every day.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，兩朝實錄成，復賜金幣、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, when the Veritable Records of the two reigns were completed, gold and coins, saddles and horses were again bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 5, when the Veritable Records of the two reigns were completed, he was again given gold, coins, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 旦入謝，歸而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the morning he entered to give thanks; returning home he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He went in that morning to give thanks, returned home, and died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚忠靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous title Loyal and Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the title Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 敕戶部復其家，世世無所與。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Revenue Ministry to restore his household, generation after generation without levies upon them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to restore his household to its former standing, exempting his descendants from levies forever.

sentences.zh: 原吉有雅景，人莫能測其際。

translations.literal: Yuanji had generous breadth; no one could fathom its limits.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji was magnanimous beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 同列有善，即采納之。

translations.literal: When colleagues had something good, he immediately adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: When colleagues had good ideas, he adopted them at once.

sentences.zh: 或有小過，必為之掩覆。

translations.literal: If they had small faults, he always covered them for them.
translations.idiomatic: If they slipped, he always covered for them.

sentences.zh: 吏汙所服金織賜衣。

translations.literal: A clerk stained the gold-woven robe bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk stained one of his gold-woven court robes.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「勿怖，汙可浣也。

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "Do not be afraid; stains can be washed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said, "Do not be afraid; stains can be washed out.

sentences.zh: 」又有汙精微文書者，吏叩頭請死。

translations.literal: There was also one who stained a subtle and refined document; the clerk kowtowed and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: When another clerk ruined an important document, the man kowtowed and begged for death.

sentences.zh: 原吉不問，自入朝引咎，帝命易之。

translations.literal: Yuanji did not inquire; he himself entered court and took the blame, and the emperor ordered it replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji said nothing; he went to court himself to accept blame, and the emperor ordered a replacement.

sentences.zh: 呂震嘗傾原吉。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen once tried to bring Yuanji down.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen had once tried to undermine Xia Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 震為子乞官，原吉以震在「靖難」時有守城功，為之請。

translations.literal: When Zhen begged an office for his son, Yuanji, because Zhen had merit in defending the city during the Pacification, pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Zhen asked an office for his son, Xia Yuanji pleaded for him, citing Lü Zhen's merit in defending the city during the civil war.

sentences.zh: 平江伯陳瑄初亦惡原吉，原吉顧時時稱瑄才。

translations.literal: The Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, at first also disliked Yuanji, yet Yuanji would from time to time praise Xuan's talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, had also disliked him at first, yet Xia Yuanji often praised Chen Xuan's abilities.

sentences.zh: 或問原吉：「量可學乎？

translations.literal: Someone asked Yuanji: "Can magnanimity be learned?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Xia Yuanji, "Can magnanimity be learned?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾幼時，有犯未嘗不怒。

translations.literal: He said: "In my youth, when someone offended me I never failed to grow angry.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "When I was young I always grew angry when offended.

sentences.zh: 始忍於色，中忍於心，久則無可忍矣。

translations.literal: At first I bore it in my expression, then in my heart; after long practice there was nothing I could not bear.
translations.idiomatic: At first I hid it in my face, then in my heart; in time there was nothing I could not bear.

sentences.zh: 」嘗夜閱爰書，撫案而嘆，筆欲下輒止。

translations.literal: Once at night he reviewed capital-case records, stroked the desk and sighed, and when the brush was about to descend he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once at night, reviewing death-sentence cases, he stroked his desk and sighed, his brush poised but unable to descend.

sentences.zh: 妻問之。

translations.literal: His wife asked him about it.
translations.idiomatic: His wife asked why.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此歲終大辟奏也。

translations.literal: He said: "This is the year-end memorial on great executions.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This is the year-end report on capital sentences.

sentences.zh: 」與同列飲他所，夜歸值雪，過禁門，有欲不下者，原吉曰：「君子不以冥冥墮行。

translations.literal: Drinking at another's house with colleagues, he returned at night in snow; passing the forbidden gate, some wished not to dismount; Yuanji said: "The gentleman does not let his conduct fall in the dark.
translations.idiomatic: Returning late from drinking with colleagues in the snow, some wished not to dismount at the forbidden gate; Xia Yuanji said, "A gentleman does not let his conduct slip in the dark.

sentences.zh: 」其慎如此。

translations.literal: Such was his caution.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his scrupulousness.

sentences.zh: 原吉與義皆起家太祖時。

translations.literal: Yuanji and Yi both rose from humble beginnings in the time of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji and Jian Yi both began their careers under Taizu.

sentences.zh: 義秉銓政，原吉筦度支，皆二十七年，名位先於三楊。

translations.literal: Yi held the power of personnel selection, Yuanji managed revenue and expenditure; each for twenty-seven years, their fame and rank preceded the Three Yangs.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi held personnel power and Xia Yuanji managed finances, each for twenty-seven years, ranking before the Three Yangs.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣之世，外兼臺省，內參館閣，與三楊同心輔政。

translations.literal: In the eras of Ren and Xuan, outwardly they concurrently held censorate and provincial posts, inwardly they participated in the Hanlin institutes, and with the Three Yangs shared one heart in assisting government.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ren and Xuan they held censorate and provincial posts abroad and advised from the Hanlin within, governing in concert with the Three Yangs.

sentences.zh: 義善謀，榮善斷，而原吉與士奇尤持大體，有古大臣風烈。

translations.literal: Yi was skilled in planning, Rong in decision, while Yuanji and Shiqi especially upheld the larger pattern and had the wind and fierce integrity of great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi excelled at planning, Yang Rong at decision, while Xia Yuanji and Yang Shiqi especially upheld the larger interest and bore the manner of great ministers of old.

sentences.zh: 子瑄，以蔭為尚寶司丞。

translations.literal: His son Xuan, through hereditary privilege, became Vice Director of the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan became a vice director in the Directorate of Ceremonial through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 喜談兵。

translations.literal: He delighted in discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to talk about military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景泰時，數上章言兵事，有沮者，不獲用。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai era he repeatedly memorialized on military affairs; some obstructed him and he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingtai Emperor he repeatedly memorialized on military affairs, but opponents blocked him and his proposals were never adopted.

sentences.zh: 終南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 李文郁，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Li Wenyu was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenyu was from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，以戶部侍郎副原吉治水有勞。

translations.literal: Early in Yongle, as Vice Minister of Revenue assisting Yuanji in water control, he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he served as Vice Minister of Revenue under Xia Yuanji on waterworks and performed with distinction.

sentences.zh: 後坐事謫遼東二十年。

translations.literal: Later, because of an affair, he was banished to Liaodong for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was banished to Liaodong for twenty years after an offense.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，召還，為南京通政參議，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was recalled, made Administration Vice Commissioner at Nanjing in the Office of Transmission, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong came to the throne he was recalled, made a vice commissioner in the Nanjing Office of Transmission, and retired.

sentences.zh: 鄒師顏，宣都人。

translations.literal: Zou Shiyan was a man of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Shiyan was from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，為江西參政，坐事免。

translations.literal: Early in Yongle he was Administration Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi and was dismissed because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he served as administration vice commissioner of Jiangxi and was dismissed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋以薦擢御史，有直聲。

translations.literal: Before long, on recommendation he was promoted to censor and had a reputation for bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recommended and made a censor, earning a reputation for blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 遷大理丞，署戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Minister of Justice and signed for the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant minister of justice and signed ministry documents for the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與原吉同下獄。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned together with Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned together with Xia Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，釋為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was released and made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong came to the throne he was released and made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 省墓歸，還至通州，卒，貧不能歸葬。

translations.literal: Returning from tending his parents' tombs, he reached Tongzhou on the way back and died; he was too poor to return his body for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from tending his parents' graves, he reached Tongzhou on the way home and died, too poor to afford burial transport.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震聞於朝，宣宗命驛舟送之。

translations.literal: Minister Lü Zhen reported this at court; Emperor Xuanzong ordered a relay boat to send the body back.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lü Zhen reported this at court, and Emperor Xuanzong ordered a courier boat to return his body.

sentences.zh: 詔京官卒者，皆給驛，著為令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that when capital officials died, relay transport should all be provided, and this was established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict provided relay transport for all capital officials who died away from home, and this became permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《書》曰「敷求哲人，俾輔於爾後嗣」。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: The Book says, "Broadly seek wise men to assist your later successors."
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The Book of Documents says, "Seek wise men broadly to assist your successors."

sentences.zh: 蹇義、夏原吉自筮仕之初，即以誠篤幹濟受知太祖，至成祖，益任以繁劇。

translations.literal: Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji from the beginning of their divined service were known to Taizu for sincere devotion and practical ability; reaching Chengzu, they were entrusted all the more with tangled and pressing duties.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of their careers Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji won Taizu's trust through sincerity and practical ability; under the Yongle Emperor they were entrusted with ever heavier duties.

sentences.zh: 而二人實能通達政體，諳練章程，稱股肱之任。

translations.literal: Yet the two men truly could penetrate the structure of governance and were thoroughly versed in regulations, worthy to be called arms and thighs in office.
translations.idiomatic: Both truly understood how government worked and knew regulations inside out, worthy of the name right-hand men.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣繼體，委寄優隆，同德協心，匡翼令主。

translations.literal: Ren and Xuan succeeded to the body politic; trust and favor were lofty; with one virtue and joined hearts they aided and winged an excellent sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ren and Xuan they enjoyed the highest trust, working in concert to support excellent rulers.

sentences.zh: 用使吏治修明，民風和樂，成績懋著，蔚為宗臣。

translations.literal: By this they caused official governance to be cultivated and clear, the people's customs harmonious and joyful, achievements splendidly manifest, and rose as pillar ministers of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: They helped make governance clear, the people content, and achievements splendid, rising to become pillar ministers of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 樹人之效，遠矣哉。

translations.literal: The effect of nurturing men—how far-reaching!
translations.idiomatic: How far-reaching is the effect of nurturing worthy men!
